text: Even in the aspect of face masks, I think Singapore may be the only country in the world to ensure that every citizen, every household, has some face masks at their home.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Those who mock them – purveyors of false news, socially irresponsible, the boors of society.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Most of all, the Budget is for the ordinary men and women of Singapore who are decent and care for our fellowmen, who would work together to stem out the foul storm that is facing Singapore.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This Budget has something for us all, and I thank the Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat and his team for their inclusive and thoughtful rendering that is this Unity Budget.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But while our nation unites to tackle the pandemic, we must not forget that long-term structural challenges, such as the declining support for globalisation, an ageing workforce and the uncertainties surrounding our economy, continue to persist.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: More worryingly, some of these challenges are now being accelerated due to COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, more can be done to help our professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs), which according to a 2019 report published by the Development Bank of Singapore Senior Economist, Irvin Seah, PMETs are now the "new vulnerables" among our workforce.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My speech today will focus on how we can help vulnerable PMETs stay employed, be more employable and help those who are feeling “sandwiched” financially.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is a timely move as PMETs in this age group are arguably at one of the most vulnerable stages in their careers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And they are vulnerable in the two key areas of employment and employability.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Employment data over the past decade has shown that PMETs are increasingly at risk of being retrenched.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This upward trend is unlikely to be reversed anytime soon and will be accelerated in the event of an economic downturn.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: PMETs, particularly those in their mid-career, are also vulnerable in terms of employability.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Those who do not keep their skillsets current will find it hard to secure new jobs when they are displaced.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat noted in his Budget speech, many of our mid-career PMETs grew up in a time when it is seen as the norm to stay in one company for life until retirement.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, with technology cycles shorter than ever, many are now at risk of being displaced by fresh graduates if they do not equip themselves with new technical and new technology skills.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Quantitatively, we are already seeing this trend happening.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If we analyse the rate of re-entry into employment among retrenched residents from MOM's Labour Market Survey, it shows that workers aged 40 and above have lower re-entry rates than their younger counterparts.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, how then, can we better support this group of vulnerable mid-career PMETs to have better job security, and boost their employability if and when they get displaced?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am proposing three strategies: (a) build a strong ecosystem of job security support within each sector; (b) bring training closer to our mid-career PMETs; and (c) equip them with adaptive skills beyond technical and technology skills.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, in the longer term, we need to ensure that our economic sectors are self-sustaining.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In my view, the concept of JSC which the NTUC Secretary-General Mr Ng Chee Meng had highlighted in his speech earlier, is a useful way forward.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: By creating a structure to formalise the matching of displaced workers in an affected sector to a growing sector in need of manpower, we will be able to achieve a more resilient employment landscape.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The NTUC JSC will benefit all working professionals and will go a long way towards mitigating the increased risk of retrenchments that our PMETs face in today’s fast-changing operating environment.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am, therefore, glad to see such strong support during the pilot phase and I urge more companies to come on board this initiative.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: To do so, we must bring training closer in terms of relevance, cost and location.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, we need to make training more relevant to our PMETs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: From my weekly visits to workplaces, many PMETs have told me that while they understood the importance of going for training and staying current with industry trends, they are unable to see how going for generic courses can help them in their specific line of work.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is why the NTUC, through its affiliated unions, has initiated the formation of CTCs with our unionised companies.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These CTCs are meant to help our workers answer the two common questions of "Train what?" and "Train for what?" Through CTCs, we work with companies to assess their specific business and operational needs and translate these needs into a targeted training plan for employees to close the skills gap and, at the same time, remain employable.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the area of cost, training must be made more affordable and within the financial reach of our PMETs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In previous Budgets, my fellow Labour Members of Parliament and I had called for top-ups to the SkillsFuture Credit and we are glad that this suggestion has been adopted.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope that the Government can expand this to include all Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) courses as well as programmes to help our PMETs to deep-skill themselves.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Deep-skill training programmes require a certain level of experience as a prerequisite and are often more costly due to their small niche.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Perhaps the Government can consider mapping deep-skill training courses to the proficiency levels found in the Skills Framework and allow eligible programmes to be further subsidised.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This way, we can help to reduce the out-of-pocket expenses for those who wish to gain a deeper mastery of their profession.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Just as we should support those who wish to continue working beyond 60, we should also support them in their pursuit of lifelong learning.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We should disburse the additional SkillsFuture Credit sooner rather than later so that our workers can attend the necessary training during this near-term economic lull and be equipped with new skills and confidence when our respective industries recover.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Beyond cost, we need to bring the training programmes physically closer to our mid-career PMETs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For courses that require a physical premises, schools, IHLs and even neighbourhood Community Centres (CCs) serve as a more convenient location for our working people to go and upgrade themselves.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Labour Movement will do our part to bring training closer to our working professionals.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Currently, the U PME Centre sits at the NTUC Members Hub in One Marina Boulevard, helping to equip PMET union members with a growth mindset through services, such as career development workshops and job preparation courses.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The existing centre has done well, serving over 1,500 individuals in the past three years.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Moving forward, we will bring these workshops and training programmes closer to our PMETs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I understand the grassroot advisor has been most supportive of this.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We will gradually extend our services to all 11 CCs located within the Tanjong Pagar Group Representation Constituency.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope that the Government can partner us to progressively open all CCs and even the Residents' Committee (RC) Centres to the mobile U PME Centre so that we, the Labour Movement, can deliver our programmes closer to the heartlands.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Skills, such as project management and communication, are becoming more in demand.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We will also work with ClickInsight, a digital marketing firm, to provide free digital marketing workshops.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: NTUC will continue working with our professional associations to expand the range of our adaptive skills training.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I urge all PMETs to sign up as an NTUC member to enjoy access to these workshops and to also tap on the yearly $250 union training subsidy, which can be added onto your SkillsFuture Credit top-ups to improve your own employability.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many PMETs find themselves "sandwiched" financially as they have both young children and elderly parents to care for.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is, therefore, important that we help them navigate through this period and emerge with sound financial footing so that they can achieve their desired quality of life during retirement.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Labour Movement has been doing our part to support workers in financial planning.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: MoneyOwl, one of our new social enterprises, was created to offer comprehensive and conflict-free advice to families and help them plan for their retirement needs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Since it was formed in 2018, MoneyOwl has benefited more than 5,000 people.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This tool incorporates the use of the various CPF schemes and provides workers with an analysis of their financial health, including gaps in their insurance protection and investments, based on their own individual risk profile.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Moving forward, NTUC will partner the Financial Planning Association of Singapore to run complimentary financial planning workshops for our union members.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These workshops will be made available through the mobile U PME Centre to benefit more PMETs and their families.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Labour Movement, through the good work of our social enterprises, such as NTUC FairPrice, will continue to do our part and do our best to help moderate the cost of living in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Through the Consumers Association of Singapore, we have also launched tools, such as Price Kaki and Fuel Kaki, to help consumers compare prices of essential household goods, hawker food and fuel.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I urge everyone to tap on these resources to get more bang for your buck.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: COVID-19 can serve as an opportunity amid a public health and economic crisis.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I call on employers to use the resources presented at this Budget as a springboard to position your businesses and our workers to ride the waves of recovery.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We can also do more to equip our PMETs with the right financial planning skills and help them in their journey towards better retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The theme for this year's Budget "Advancing as One Singapore" reminds us that when we work as one, we can overcome any challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our frontline workers who have been working tirelessly around the clock in our fight against COVID-19 and the many ground-up initiatives and responses from the community rallying behind them embody the strong Singapore spirit that will see us through any challenge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To our doctors, nurses and healthcare workers, our cleaning and security personnel, public officers and all our frontline workers, thank you.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The manufacturing and service sectors are also facing a manpower squeeze as many workers from China are unable to return to Singapore yet for work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This adds extra pressure or our already tight labour market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some may experience an even greater drop in demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While support measures have been extended to sectors, such as those that are most immediately affected by COVID-19, I hope that the Government can pay special attention to sectors that may feel the downstream ripple effects of COVID-19, especially if the situation is protracted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is well received by many of my union leaders and workers, who told me that while they are worried about the impact of COVID-19 on their job security, they are thankful that JSS and the Wage Credit Scheme will help enterprises retain their workers and protect the jobs that they have.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Protecting the jobs of our workers will also allow our companies to retain their critical manpower capabilities, so they can respond swiftly when the DORSCON level normalises and the economy picks up again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Labour Movement supports the Budget measures in the Stabilisation and Support Package.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our unions have been working closely with their management partners over the last few weeks to see how best they can utilise the downtime to reskill workers, especially those whose jobs have been impacted by COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Working with the Food, Drinks and Allied Workers Union (FDAWU), the hotel's General Manager, Mr Kung Teong Wah, saw value in tapping on the Hotel Job Redesign Place-and-Train programme to multi-skill their workers in other job functions so that they can actually be cross-deployed into other departments when there is a shortage of manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: He even took the initiative to convince general managers from other hotels within the same group to do likewise in order to avoid asking their workers to go on mandatory annual leave or to take no-pay leave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is just one of the first-movers from our unionised companies who is taking the lead to send workers for training during this downturn and I hope that more companies will also seize the opportunity to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, some companies and workers have expressed difficulties navigating the huge number of courses available for skills training and, therefore, are unsure of how to select the courses appropriate for their needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They found it difficult to map the type of training to the specific skills in the skills framework that are promulgated by SkillsFuture Singapore and hope that the training they received could be better recognised by employers as well as the industry towards their career progression.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There is a need for Government agencies to work with tripartite partners as well as HR practitioners to streamline the approach and make the "customer journey" of lifelong learning a much easier one to navigate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will complement the Government's efforts in providing more SkillsFuture Credits at both the individual and enterprise levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For companies that are keen to train their workers but are unable to find courses due to training gaps currently available in the industry, NTUC LearningHub stands ready to work with companies to bridge the gap and strengthen training in the respective sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In coping with COVID-19, many companies have also implemented their Business Continuity Plans (BCPs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many have split team arrangements to minimise the risks of community spread while ensuring operational continuity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In place of face-to-face meetings or discussions, the teams now meet virtually over their smart phones or laptops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Companies can take this opportunity to help these workers transit and become more digitally confident and, at the same time, use this as impetus to accelerate the digital transformation of their business processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Through the use of technology and job redesign, flexi-work arrangements (FWAs) for certain jobs can, indeed, be a more permanent arrangement to save on operating costs like office rental and utilities while providing the opportunity for employees to remain productive and empowered to manage their time flexibly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This can also meet the needs of many working mothers to balance their childcaring needs and career aspirations while contributing positively to our labour force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, it is in a crisis where we must make the full use of it to push ourselves to transform even faster.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In coping with the near-term challenges brought about by COVID-19, our companies should, therefore, not forget about the long-term goal of growing and expanding their businesses through deeper industry transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Labor Movement has been advocating the formation of CTCs to help drive companies' transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Allow me to share a little bit more about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This helps our companies to systematically map out the process of using technology, process change, work redesign and workers' training to turn their strategic business objectives into concrete, tangible, actionable items.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some CTCs have already completed the OTR process and are pushing ahead with their transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Energizer, a unionised company, a household name under the United Workers of Electronics and Electrical Industries (UWEEI), is one such example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our union leader, Sister Sukartini, who is the Branch Chair of UWEEI in Energizer, was involved in the whole OTR process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Because she was able to give critical inputs about workers' concerns and understanding of the ground situation, this has helped the company's management to identify gaps and blindspots in the roadmap.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The OTR process has certainly helped Energizer to identify transformation priorities and action plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: CTC will be the platform for regular tracking of their transformation objectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Apart from MNCs, SMEs are also leveraging the CTC platform and the OTR process to systematically transform their businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Fong's Engineering is an SME unionised under the Metal Industries Workers' Union.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I have shared in previous Budget speeches before how Fong's has embraced innovation and business model transformation very much early on to help keep themselves ahead of the competition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While having done their own company planning previously, Fong's still chose to undertake the OTR process in November last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The aim is to re-evaluate the relevance of their previous transformation plans and, through this OTR process, Fong's managed to pinpoint some blindspots in their current transformation plan that needed a further in-depth analysis, they identified additional talent and training needs and updated their transformation plan to move even more decisively for the next two years ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, whether you are an MNC or an SME, let me encourage all companies to work with our Labour Movement via the CTC platform to hasten and deepen your transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Through the CTCs, the unions work closely with the companies and relevant agencies in the Government to tap on the various support measures and resources to make the company transformation and the workers' training a reality.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: (In Mandarin):   With the reduction in workload during this lull period, EDG as well as the SkillsFuture Enterprise Grant can be used to help companies redesign jobs and enhance the skills of their workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They can focus on business transformation, respond quickly and seize new opportunities when the economy recovers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In the past few weeks, NTUC and our management partners have been working closely to see how we can make full use of the lull period to upskill workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Currently, there are many skills upgrading courses in the market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, with so many different courses to choose from, some companies and workers are at a loss about which courses to pick.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They also find it difficult to map the training courses against the skills framework developed by SkillsFuture Singapore, and hope that the training they have undergone will be better recognised by their employers and the industry, and that it will help advance their career.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Government Ministries and agencies need to work with their tripartite partners and HR professionals to streamline the matching of courses with the skills framework, and make the “customer experience” of lifelong learning more manageable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will fit in better with the Government’s efforts to provide more SkillsFuture Credits at the individual and enterprise levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To manage the operational risks of COVID-19, many companies have rolled out business continuity plans, adopted segregated work arrangements and allowed some workers to telecommute using their laptops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I hope that companies and workers will ride on the momentum driven by this crisis to deepen and accelerate the pace of transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Labour Movement is committed to partner the Government and employers to work towards a brighter future for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Labour Movement stands ready to work with the Government and our employers to Advance as One Singapore and build a stronger and better future for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The Budget reflects the values and priorities of our citizens and charts the direction to deploy our limited financial resources to meet our nation's goals and objectives.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: A substantial Budget amount has been put aside for Health, Education and measures that address climate change.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The Deputy Prime Minister spoke on another critical aspect of the Budget that is of importance to the workers of Singapore, that is, on transforming our industries and workforce.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore went through a major industrial transformation in the 1970s and the Government of the day then stepped up training of the workforce to handle new jobs that came into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Fifty years have gone by and we are now at the crossroads of change.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, it will help our workers to stay in their jobs and to go for skills upgrading.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: But may I seek clarification from the Minister as to the reasons for the short duration of the support?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: What happens, God forbid, if the COVID-19 outbreak stays around longer?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Also, companies do need time to adjust even after COVID-19 is over.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: How do we ensure that companies that benefited from these subsidies will not let go of their workers after the support ends?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Yesterday, MOM announced the introduction of a temporary scheme to help the manufacturing and services sectors manage their manpower needs.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: MOM will allow businesses in these sectors with excess foreign workforce to transfer their workers to companies with a manpower shortage.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: While I support the move, can the Government go further and consider reducing foreign worker levies for firms affected by COVID-19, similar to what was in place during the 2003 SARS period?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Under the Transformation and Growth strategy, there are three key thrusts, of which, developing our people is one.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: This aims to enable our citizens to get better jobs, better wages and to stay employable.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The new SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit and the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package aim to do that.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: It is a welcome move as both companies and workers benefit.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: It will encourage the companies to send their workers for training and skills upgrading and, at the same time, workers will benefit in terms of their employability.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: My main concern is the implementation of these schemes.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: In many sectors, a portion of workers' monthly pay comprises variables, such as operational incentives, overtime or shift allowances.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Workers will have to forego these variable payments to attend training to undertake new or additional roles.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: In some cases, these variables can be as high as one third of their monthly gross pay, if not more.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The Labour Movement calls on employers not to shortchange employees and to share the productivity gains fairly while recognising workers who support the company's transformation through skills upgrading at the expense of undertaking short-term pay reduction.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: This gesture will strengthen the trust between employers and their workers while ensuring the workforce is well-equipped and future-ready.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: At the last National Day Rally, the Prime Minister announced raising the retirement age to 65 and re-employment age to 70 in phases by the end of the decade.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The Labour Movement has since then called on companies to move forward the implementation date before the law comes into place.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Unfortunately, many are reluctant, citing cost as a significant factor.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The Labour Movement hopes there is less of an excuse now to hold back but to move forward to our call.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The Senior Employment Credit and the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant, together with the CPF Transition Offset, will help companies manage the overall wage cost.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: I urge employers to not view these workers as cost burden but as valuable assets with tacit knowledge, for these senior employees will be the ones mentoring the next generation of workers.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: On that note, there are some groups of senior employees that the companies are reluctant to extend their retirement and re-employment age.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: They are mainly the general administrative staff who are easily replaceable with younger employees as their wage cost is lower and with employees in specific roles where physical fitness is a requirement.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Technologies, such as robotic process automation (RPA), execute repetitive business processes cheaper, faster and without human errors.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: As such technologies become more pervasive in workplaces, office-based generalist staff become vulnerable and face more reduced opportunities for re-employment when they retire.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The Labour Movement calls on employers to intervene early through career planning customised to individual employees' needs and profiles.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The companies can consider reskilling them in their 40s to achieve better job security and job progression when they retire and seek re-employment in the company.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: This reskilling reframes one's mindset and gets them prepared for the change.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Budget 2020 is a step in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The Deputy Prime Minister's call resonates with the Labour Movement.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The time is now to take action and walk the talk.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This year’s Budget intends to mitigate the short-term vulnerabilities faced by businesses and workers without taking our eyes off the future.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In the medium- and long-term horizon, the rapidly changing job market and business models can leave many workers behind if they are unprepared.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The vulnerability of workers can manifest itself in the form of stagnating wages, job insecurity, skill redundancies and poor working conditions, among many others.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While the Budget can help mitigate these vulnerabilities, a concerted effort by the tripartite partners and a mindset change in our society are still needed to alleviate some of these vulnerabilities because every worker matters and every job counts.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There are workers providing essential services that are very susceptible to low and stagnating wages and poor working conditions due to the business nature of their industry characterised by competitive biddings and undercutting.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In terms of mitigating workers' vulnerability due to low and stagnating wages, it is undeniable that the tripartite partners have done a lot to help our workers in the outsourced industries, such as cleaning, security and landscape.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Sectors like waste collection and strata management are keen to have a mandatory PWM and it is important to have Government support to identify and leverage the key levers that would encourage widespread adoption.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Lack of knowledge on what constitutes fair wages can also increase workers' vulnerability.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There are many with disabilities who are working or would like to seek employment.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, it may not be easy for them to work in a building where the physical structure may pose a big hindrance or for them to find companies that offer employment to people with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In this aspect, I would like to call for the Government to consider providing funding support to help employers offset the costs needed to modify infrastructure at workplaces, especially in older buildings, to encourage employment of people with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The various job portals, such as MyCareersFuture.sg or the National Jobs Bank, should indicate positions that welcome persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: All these measures would promote a more inclusive workforce because every worker matters and every job counts.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Workers are also vulnerable if employers cannot pay their wages because the company has ceased operations.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While these workers can lodge their salary claims with the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM), in most cases, their salaries cannot be recovered once the company has ceased operations.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We need to do more to protect our workers from failed businesses.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Currently, there is a short-term relief fund administered by the NTUC U Care Centre to help low-wage workers who are owed salaries because their companies have ceased operations.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many of these workers who are owed salaries are sole breadwinners and, for them and their families, the hardship is real and painful.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: All workers deserve to have their rice bowl protected and we must continue to explore ways to help and protect more workers.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Workers can also become vulnerable due to unfair employment contracts.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Some employers have included in employment contracts certain clauses that may not be fair to the workers, perhaps to address staff attrition, recoup losses that they incur due to liquidated damages or protect their business interests.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Regardless, including unfair clauses is unethical and they abuse the vulnerable position the workers might be in.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There needs to be greater engagement to help workers understand employment contracts and this outreach could start in our tertiary institutions.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: MOM may also want to consider starting a watchlist if companies are found or reported to have unfair clauses in their employment contracts.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Administrative penalties should be imposed on companies on this watchlist.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Tripartite partners must also work together to ensure that all Singaporeans can work with dignity.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: A tripartite advisory on the provision of rest areas for outsourced workers has been released to act as a guide for service buyers and service providers in providing proper rest areas for outsourced workers.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We would like to call on the Government to provide incentives to urge more building owners to provide rest areas for their outsourced workers.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While the Government has given hiring incentives for employers to hire local mature workers, the efforts to enlighten employers to have a truly inclusive workforce must continue.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I am also equally heartened with the Senior Worker Support Package for older workers to reduce their employment vulnerability.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Regardless of one’s age group, every worker matters and every job counts.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In English): Every Budget must provide funding and resources to help workers reduce their vulnerabilities.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We need to work together to reduce workers' vulnerabilities and to show we care for the workers.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While I call upon employers to uphold their responsibilities to their workers and to do more for their welfare and well-being, I would also like to remind workers, all my fellow workers, to take charge of their career development and be future-ready.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: All of us have a part to play in creating an inclusive and caring society where every worker matters and every job counts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Measures, such as the Job Support Scheme and the Wage Credit Scheme, will reassure workers that the Government is helping to secure jobs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Amidst the immediate needs to mitigate against the adverse impact of COVID-19 outbreak, it is easy to lose sight of our longer-term imperatives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is understandable as immediate survival is key.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This outbreak has also highlighted the problems of being dependent on a large economy or being interconnected with multiple economies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Do we now need to re-examine our strategies and adjust course, rather than doing more of the same?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: With its obvious focus on the COVID-19 economic fallout, how are we still ensuring that we are funding our social strategies in education, healthcare and housing to ensure equal opportunities for all?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is critical that we need to stay true to what has made Singapore successful – equal opportunities for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Being a comprehensive Budget, it would almost be nitpicking to find gaps.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The COVID-19 outbreak highlights the precarious situation of Self-Employed Persons (SEPs).

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Many SEPs were and still are adversely affected, not only those in the hospitality-related industries but also those in the creative, events, sporting, outdoor learning and transport industries.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But most of the Budget 2020 measures are channelled through companies, and our SEPs might not be helped.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: They also have limited medical and training support except those provided via SkillsFuture.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Those dependent on platforms, such as Grab food delivery riders, have an imbalance of bargaining powers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We often hear of adjustments to incentive structures unilaterally without consultation with SEPs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This would probably not have happened, or to a lesser extent, in a typical employer-employee structure.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The way forward is not one of absolute parity with traditional employees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: SEPs do treasure the flexibility of contract work.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Both of these approaches are not without their limitation but it certainly betters the lot of the SEPs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I hope that the Ministry can also consider providing greater support for SEPs in the second phase of COVID-19 support, if ever one is needed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Next, on the unmet needs of the younger workforce.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Our Young NTUC survey showed that younger Singaporeans are keen to develop themselves overseas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The Asia Ready Exposure Programme in Budget 2020 would greatly help our students to pick up those valuable experiences while still in school.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We also hope that young Singaporeans in their first or second career can also have such opportunities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Especially those in their early 20s, there is still sufficient runway for an internship.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: However, the resources available to them are limited.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Those Singaporeans who have graduated are dependent on their companies for overseas exposure.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Government provide a one-stop centre and perhaps subsidies for younger Singaporeans to explore careers in Asia, especially Southeast Asia?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Next, let me discuss on the gender wage gap.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is not a common Budget Debate topic.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But first, it is an important issue and second, there are opportunities afforded from the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Yet, it still runs counter to the principle that all things being equal, men and women must obtain the same pay if they are doing the same job with similar outcomes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And we also acknowledge that absolute gender parity in job outcomes is not necessarily a normative ideal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But there is immense value to pursue the economic outcomes of greater equality, besides addressing the social issues and the values that we engender as a nation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Indeed, there are benefits for greater women participation at all levels.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In an IMF blog piece by Christine Lagarde and Johnathan Ostry on 28 November 2018, their conclusion was gender diversity matters.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I quote, "Our analysis springs from the observation – supported by considerable microeconomic evidence – that women and men bring different skills and perspectives to the workplace, including different attitudes to risk and collaboration.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: There are structural issues to tackle: first, HR, and how we grade women who are out on maternity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: A working mother would be entitled to up to 16 weeks of Government-Paid Maternity Leave.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But oftentimes, in some organisations, they might be graded on the same 12 months as any other colleagues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This meant that from a work output perspective, the women on maternity leave are already at a disadvantage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Companies would argue that it would only be fair to the other colleagues who picked up the slack.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But this also meant that good talent on maternity would not be given a level playing field to progress as progression are usually based on consistency of better graded performances.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This has perhaps contributed to a lack of women in senior leadership positions over time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Second, we see a persistent lack of women at the top leadership positions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Perhaps having a more diverse leadership might provide for better gender-neutral policies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Third, some women decide to leave the workforce entirely because of a lack of supportive workplace measures, such as FWAs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Women are still often expected to take on the primary role at home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Normalising FWA options give a degree of comfort to working women, as it helps working caregivers avoid the conflict they face in trying to balance their careers with responsibilities at home, something especially accentuated post-maternity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It can be very difficult to ask a woman to ask for FWA if it is seen as a privilege and not a norm.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The COVID-19 outbreak has clearly shown that organisations can and are able to operate with broad FWA, even as we speak now.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Previously, the argument was it was not possible.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Planning from the start meant that women will still be able to have a more level promotion path after maternity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Citigroup, for example, has adjusted the pay in Singapore of women who earned less than their male peers for doing the same job.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We all need to lean in to create a more inclusive environment for women.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It tackles the immediate challenges head-on without losing sight of the future transformation needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: No Budget is expected to address all issues, which is why we must also view each Budget as part of a larger whole.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is a longer financial plan after all.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The COVID-19 episode requires significant shift of resources but it is necessary.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: COVID-19 will also eventually come to pass if we are united.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And we must be ready when the upturn opportunities present themselves.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Notwithstanding my earlier suggestions, I support the Motion.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   The sudden onset of COVID-19 has dealt a serious blow to our economy.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Not knowing how long this epidemic will last, many Singaporeans are worried that their livelihoods will be seriously affected and they might lose their jobs.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Nevertheless, with the previous experience of fighting SARS, most Singaporeans were not panicky when COVID-19 struck.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the contrary, we could face this challenge calmly.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The greatest test is not whether we are able to stock up groceries or whether we can adopt healthier habits, but whether we are able to display confidence and a cooperative spirit to fight this disease.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Undoubtedly, self-preservation can only ensure that we and our families are protected temporarily.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But in the long run, it will not protect our national economy, companies or job situation.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To deal with the impact of COVID-19, we need to work together and make full use of the Government measures provided in the Budget.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Fortunately, most drivers are still working as usual.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They do not complain but hope that there will be adequate solutions or packages to help them tide over this period.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On normal days, there is already intense competition between taxi drivers and private hire drivers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Fortunately, when COVID-19 hit us, the tripartite partners consisting of unions, the Government and employers worked together like "plywood".

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Plywood can take on much heavier loads than an individual layer of wood.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Each layer of plywood may be made of different materials and differ in terms of quality, but when bound together as plywood, the effect is very significant.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The spread of COVID-19 has brought about stern challenges.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although we cannot proclaim to have solved every problem easily, at least we have been able to come up with measures as the situation evolved.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: During the initial stage, unions took the initiative to understand the concerns of our taxi drivers, and most drivers expressed hope that they can drive their cars safely but said they lacked protective supplies like hand sanitisers and disinfectants.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Since then, unions have tried their best to procure these necessities for drivers through various channels and distributed the supplies to them.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Government and operators have also provided necessary resources and helped drivers to monitor their body temperature, so as to give customers peace of mind.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We have also used our funds to help drivers who had to stop driving due to quarantine orders, so that they can tide over this difficult period.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, workers from the PTP transport sector are able to receive help from the Government and operators with swift and targeted measures.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Only with this "plywood" cooperative spirit are we able to help workers keep their jobs and keep companies going.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Only a strong enterprise, a resilient labour force, a thoughtful and efficient union, and a nation with wit and resources can ensure the job security of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Job security means that the economy, companies and workers must receive appropriate support, and establish close partnerships where everyone works to help one another.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As we know, a lot of things are easier said than done.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our tripartite partners have been working together to stabilise the economy while continuing to help transform industries and assist workers in training, so that they can upgrade their skills, keep their jobs and tide over this difficult time.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: During this period, I have witnessed how taxi drivers and private hire drivers turn from competitors to cooperative partners.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They volunteer to distribute masks and hand sanitisers to colleagues and help them to do temperature checks.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although there has been talk that frontline healthcare workers are being discriminated by members of the public, many of our taxi drivers have volunteered to ferry healthcare workers to and from work.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: All of us have chosen to help one another in this crisis period and to weather the storm together.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Each party has put aside their different views and corporate brand names, with the single objective of consolidating the economy and development of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Once again, I would like to thank the Finance Minister for giving a booster shot to the PTP transport industry.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our tour guides have also just received help from the Government, and the tripartite partners are working to assist them.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have reached out to several freelancers to understand their situation and discuss ways to help them.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They include sports coaches, instructors, technicians, performers and photographers and so on.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that the Government Ministries can take the lead and work with industry players to think of ways to help them reduce cost and expand customer base.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In fact, some taxi drivers have urged me to organise an activity for everyone to eat beehoon together.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some Hokkien taxi drivers joked that we will "wun wun jia beehoon" (eat beehoon calmly).

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, I hope that we can be strong and steady, and not be overly worried.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is the greatest help that we can give to all our industries and all our workers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Let us work together and show determination in adversity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: At Budget Debate 2018, I called for tripartite discussions to determine the new longer-term retirement and re-employment ages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: At last year's Budget Debate, I expressed the hope that the Tripartite Workgroup formed by MOM in May 2018 to negotiate higher retirement and re-employment ages and enhanced CPF contribution rates would soon come to a win-win outcome so that older workers would have added confidence about their employment and retirement savings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As Singapore's population is ageing, progress in these areas is necessary and important to help sustain the added years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The agreement that we reached shows the strength of our tripartism to tackle real and serious issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It also showed the Government's commitment towards looking after the interests of our older workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, on behalf of older workers, I thank the Government and the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF) for working hand in hand with NTUC to achieve these win-win outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: A year has passed and we are now in Budget Debate 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Since January this year, the Singapore economy has been buffeted by the negative disruptive effects of the COVID-19 virus outbreak internationally even as the downsides of the US-China trade war continue to slow global trade and growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Against this background, Singapore's growth forecast has been revised downwards significantly, from between 0.5% and 2.5% that was estimated in November last year, to between -0.5% and 1.5% in February this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, within these months, it was revised downwards significantly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: On the ground, these changes in projections reflect falling demand, supply chain and manpower disruptions, as well as cost, credit and cash flow pressures and worries for companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And these worries for companies, in turn, translate into worker concerns over loss of overtime and other forms of income, wage freezes and even cuts, and increasing anxiety over the security of their jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Older workers, both executives and non-executives, feel vulnerable in this environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: They are afraid that in any industry or company shakeout, they may bear the brunt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: They are also worried that if they are displaced from their jobs, it would be more difficult for them to find new work or to expect to maintain anything near their original pay levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And if that happens, then it would erode the progress of prior efforts to strengthen the sustainability of our ageing population over the long run.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Older workers, therefore, look to the Government and to this Budget for reassurance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: They hope to see and they want to trust that this Government will continue to have their backs and would lean forward to safeguard their interests and ensure that they are fairly treated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The Labour Movement hears their concerns and have lobbied hard on their behalf with the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This Budget, Mr Speaker, has given older workers that reassurance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And I thank the Government for understanding the worker's needs and worries, and for addressing our older workers' concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Consider the announced CPF contribution rates improvements meant for 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The worry, as expressed by older workers is that, given the headwinds and the difficult economic environment that we are facing now, they worry whether the Government would now decide to postpone or cancel those improvements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And so, when they heard the Budget, they heard that the Government has instead stepped forward to help defray the cost pressure on employers that those improved CPF rates would bring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In other words, what the Government has promised to older workers in this improved CPF rates in 2021 will be done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is the Government keeping its word to our older workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: But workers then worry that if they should lose their jobs in the meantime, or cannot find a new one if they are displaced, then improved CPF rates, or for that matter, raised retirement and employment ages, will be moot.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Hereto, the Budget has measures aimed at lowering such risks for older workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Under the Stabilisation and Support Package, the Government will introduce JSS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This JSS will help enterprises retain their local employees during this period of uncertainty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And this is on top of the Special Employment Credits and the Additional Special Employment Credits previously introduced to incentivise the hiring of older workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These two incentives, we were told, will then be combined and restructured into a new Seniors Employment Credit Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The Government will also enhance the Wage Credit Scheme to further help shoulder the cost of wage increases for workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These moves make each existing employee less costly to their companies and, therefore, lower their overall risk of retrenchment, or will help companies hold off retrenchment for as long as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: There is even another incentive for employers who are prepared to hire older workers on a part-time basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This will help make older workers who are unable to work full-time more cost-effective for employers to consider hiring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: By the sheer number of targeted subsidies and incentives aimed at sustaining and spurring continued hiring of older Singaporean workers in this Budget, the Government's care for and commitment to our older workers are crystal clear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: While keeping one's job or being able to get back into one quickly in the event of retrenchment is of immediate concern in the current economic climate, our older workers also know that their longer-term employment and employability really depend on whether they can keep up and adapt with the changing technology and business models and methods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Here, they look to the Government and the tripartite partners to do more to help them stay skilled and relevant to the changing times and requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The Government is certainly doing its part to energise skills building for the benefit of workers and companies in this Budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In terms of enabling skills building through funding, the Government is introducing the next bound of SkillsFuture through this Budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These incentives, together with substantial existing grants and subsidies from ESG, Workforce Singapore and other economic agencies, again go to show the Government's firm belief in enabling individual and corporate investment in building skills and capabilities for greater competitiveness and in enhancing the employment and employability of our workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: On the Labour Movement's part, as elaborated by my fellow Labour Member of Parliament colleagues earlier, we introduced last year the CTCs as platforms to bring companies and unions into partnership over skills building, and to inject Government resources and support for such initiatives through this channel and platform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is a practical way to proactively and systematically upgrade companies' and workers' capabilities, and to help build momentum for the overall transformation of Singapore's economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Provisions of this year's Budget can certainly give a boost to the CTCs' efforts, and I urge our tripartite partners to make full use of these resources to press ahead with investing in our workers' training across all ages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For displaced workers, finding a new job quickly is important.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is especially so for older workers as experience tells us that they will find it more difficult to find a new job and to maintain the previous pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And this affects not only what we might traditionally call rank-and-file workers, but actually, it is so for all levels and all ages of workers, affecting also middle-age PMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Such professionals will be able to find new career runways through the PCPs' skill-up-and-switch roadmaps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I fully support this, and I have one call on the Government to consider, which is to broaden the age criterion – currently set between 40 and 60 – to include those up to the current re-employment age ceiling of 67.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And the reason is because all the factors that we have argued about, the 40- to 60-year-olds having the vulnerability, they would certainly also apply from 60 to 67.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Indeed, if anything, if that group should lose their jobs, the challenges will not be less than those aged 40 to 60.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: At the same time, the scheme itself has certain safeguards in terms of useful courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, it is good and proper that we broaden the criteria to include workers up to the re-employment age ceiling of 67 and to continue in this way to show the Government's commitment towards their employment, employability and welfare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In this area of boosting job search and placement, the Government will find an enthusiastic innovator in the Labour Movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As Minister in the Prime Minister's office and Secretary-General of NTUC, brother Ng Chee Meng had said earlier that NTUC will be spearheading the JSC in partnership with industry to go beyond what, for example, NTUC's e2i has traditionally done for individual jobseekers and individual hiring companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Through proactive information sharing and planning, JSCs and CTCs can work together to efficiently facilitate training, retraining and placements between manpower-flushed areas and manpower-starved areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Such system-level efficiency in manpower redeployment will further sharpen Singapore's overall competitiveness that is good for business and it would certainly help shorten periods of unemployment for workers who are seeking new jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We have to face down both the immediate COVID-19 threat as well as shape up for the big challenges and opportunities that the future economy will bring.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: It consists of two parts, one dealing with the effects of the COVID-19 crisis meant to stabilise the economy and support those affected by the current crisis, and a second component designed to help our country continue to grow over the longer term.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: It supports a range of short-term measures to help us tide over the current crisis and a broad suite of longer-term measures to ensure that the economy continues to grow over the long term and that our people can enjoy an increasing quality of life.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: All these resonate with me, not just because they are important issues affecting the future of our country but also because I have always believed that we, as a nation, can take the global lead on these issues.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: We cannot afford to be distracted from discussing the real challenges facing our country.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: It is also important that we learn from this experience and put in place changes and preparations that can help us face the next crisis.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Our Government has responded decisively to the crisis.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: As a people, we have shown both the good and not so good behaviour during this challenging time.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: The rush for food items and sundry items, such as toilet paper, when the DORSCON level was changed from Yellow to Orange, reflected not only anxiety but also an irrational response that brought out the worst of Singaporeans.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: My thanks to all the staff of the various supermarkets and outlets for showing immense patience and fortitude during this period.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Several self-initiated efforts have emerged to rally support for our frontline workers.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Youth groups, religious and community organisations, civil society groups and several selfless individuals are all coming together to play their part in this effort.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: These and other examples of selfless Singaporeans stepping forward to do what they can to deal with this crisis are instances that should give us hope that there is the better side of us waiting to come out, especially when the need arises.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Many have also adjusted to a new normal of washing our hands regularly, staying away from crowded places, wearing a mask if we are unwell and spending time with loved ones in parks and beaches enjoying the fresh air and breeze prevalent this time of the year.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Some have also adjusted to working in different teams at different times and locations, such as their homes, and meeting only if necessary.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: And I am told by a friend that because of some working from home, Raffles Place is a lot quieter and cleaner.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Congestion in the morning seems to have eased a bit.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: If we make this change permanent, would our quality of life not improve?

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: For those with young children in school, being at home on a working day can, indeed, be helpful.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Likewise, conducting classes online has become a part of the new normal.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Coming from an IHL, I am all for online learning to be one of the features of our IHLs.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: IHLs can decide on the balance among the various classes.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Online learning will release classrooms for other needs.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Clearly, interaction between students and staff must continue, albeit for those that really warrant, it such as tutorials, project discussions and lab work.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: So, let us work together with the team and other Singaporeans in seeing the end of this current crisis as soon as possible.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: I am sure Ministers Gan Kim Yong and Lawrence Wong are both looking forward to a good night's sleep and perhaps a round of golf when all this is over.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: I look forward to meeting them at the greens.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: The rush to stock up food items over that fateful weekend reminds us that getting communications right is very important.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Today, we are inundated by news of all sorts from various platforms and from friends and strangers alike.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: The fundamental question is whether we trust the Government in telling us what is the right thing to do, especially during a crisis.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Rumours and misinformation about lack of supplies helped to fuel senseless hoarding.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Chaos could have broken out leading to unimaginable losses.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: This is something we all do not want to happen in Singapore.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: There is a sense among them that the Government is using this legislation for its own agenda rather than serving the needs of our people.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: I am all too familiar with this kind of concern.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Many groups continue to flourish on the Internet.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: All we wanted, and I am sure all of us can agree to this, is responsible behavior on the Internet, especially when the issues affect the lives of so many Singaporeans.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Consider the effects of climate change on our small island.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: It is a long-term issue which requires us to put in place the solutions now.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: It means spending valuable state resources on matters which will affect future generations but does not bring immediate benefits.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: At the same time, if other countries do not put in place their own mitigation measures, climatic changes can affect us.

speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
text: Hence, dealing with the effects of climate change will raise many questions about how the Government should best use our limited fiscal resources for the good of our country.
