text: At the end of the day, it is important to know that a lot of these things that we are doing today, we have to change.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: But I will just say that it is just a transition, it is just a change.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: If you have been selling your product from a shop, then it is time for you to think about selling it online, without the sunk costs, without additional labour, you sell it online, figuring out how to do the logistics and delivery.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I think a lot of people say "We want to do it" but, at the end of the day, they may not do it.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Most importantly is that at the end of COVID-19 or any other crisis or challenge, let us not give up.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Let us not give up on what we can do because Singapore is in a much better shape not just in tackling the COVID-19 issues, the virus itself and making sure of healthcare but business-wise as well.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I still see vibrancy in our businesses; I still see revenues rising for some of the companies.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: So, because of that, we can work together, both public and private sectors, as well as all of us in the House, to help bring this economy back up again.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, I would like to thank the 54 MPs, including all nine Nominated MPs, who rose to offer your perspectives and suggestions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I do not have 57 files; just two.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have also learnt many new terms, including Mr Lim Swee Say's H2P2 or Happy and Healthy, Productive and Purposeful; Prof Lim Sun Sun's 3Ms, which is not massively more money, but "mobility, maturity, mentality"; and Mr Ang Hin Kee's "woon woon jiak beehoon" or steadily, we eat the beehoon.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: My special thanks to Mr Liang Eng Hwa who opened the Debate as Chairman of the Government Parliamentary Committee for Finance and Trade and Industry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond this House, I also appreciate the many helpful, constructive perspectives shared by fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They have enriched the national conversation on this Budget and the issues it seeks to address.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year’s Budget takes place under exceptional circumstances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a trying moment for businesses, workers and households, having to deal with both the softening of the global economy and the sudden COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: How we respond to moments of challenge and crisis is a test of our individual resilience and the strength of our character.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even more, it is a test of our social cohesion and solidarity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a test of who we are as a people, as a nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Do we panic and become self-centred or do we stay calm, band together and look after one another?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since I delivered the Budget Statement last week, some have asked why we call it "Our Unity Budget"?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It expresses our confidence that Singaporeans will rally together to meet our challenges head-on.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It expresses our conviction that we will emerge from this test stronger, more resilient and more united than ever before.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It expresses the spirit shown by many Singaporeans – of staying united as one people through thick and thin.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond fighting the COVID-19 outbreak, our unity will be the foundation for Singaporeans to press forward and write the next chapter of the Singapore Story.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: United, we can overcome the longer-term challenges of ageing, technological disruption, social inequality and climate change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: United, we will make sure that the Singapore Story endures and goes from strength to strength.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We should not take our unity for granted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Around the world and closer to home, we have seen societies torn by forces that foment polarisation, communal conflicts and political turmoil.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These have weakened their social cohesion and the sense of togetherness that are so essential for societies to meet the complex challenges of the day.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need, as many thoughtful commentators pointed out, a whole-of-society response.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will round up this Budget Debate by addressing Members' contributions along four key themes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, how we will overcome our immediate challenges and the COVID-19 outbreak together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, how we should manage our finances collectively to provide for our future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, how we should tackle the long-term challenge of climate change and turn our constraints into strengths.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, let me speak on our present challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Having gone through SARS 17 years ago and other outbreaks like H1N1 since then, we are much better prepared for COVID-19 today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With systematic and long-term planning, we have developed new facilities, like the National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID), deepened research capabilities in health and biomedical sciences, built up our networks of experts and honed our effectiveness in contact tracing and quarantine.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Most importantly, we have well-trained and dedicated people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These capabilities are now deployed to good effect to deal with the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Although we have kept the outbreak contained so far, it has already had a significant impact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have received a wide range of feedback about the support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many are relieved that we have a strong and decisive Budget, with both broad-based and targeted support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many Members of this House have asked if we are doing enough, particularly for businesses in the sectors directly affected and those feeling the knock-on effects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the other hand, some economists have wondered if we are doing too much.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must not fight the current war simply based on the lessons of the last war.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we should, to the best of our ability, make a sound diagnosis of the current challenges and apply a decisive course of action, or as one says in Chinese, "对症下药", fit the remedy to the case.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we must bear in mind the caution that Ministers Gan Kim Yong and Lawrence Wong have given – this is a fast-moving, fluid situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While the evidence is that the impact of the COVID-19 virus is more like H1N1 than SARS, its rapid spread through places like Iran, Italy and South Korea demonstrates the fluidity of the situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must maintain a state of dynamic vigilance and be prepared to adjust course as new information comes in.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This took into account the context of the global slowdown and wider uncertainties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are applying the support to where it matters most.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The two biggest items in the Stabilisation and Support Package – the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) and the Wage Credit Scheme (WCS) – are focused on preserving and enhancing jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With greater job assurance, workers are in a better frame of mind to go for training.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will also avoid them having to cut down too much on consumption.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SMEs, which employ the bulk of local workers and whose concerns were raised by Ms Denise Phua and Mr Ong Teng Koon, are a key focus of these two schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is on top of the help they will also receive through the Corporate Income Tax Rebate and other measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we are giving support to those sectors which are most directly impacted by COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our sector-specific measures are calibrated according to the extent to which each sector has been affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Tourism, accommodation and aviation have been hit hardest and are, therefore, given additional support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will include enhanced absentee payroll support for workers, an issue that Mr Seah Kian Peng raised.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we have extended support to other groups which have felt the ripple effects, including Self-Employed Persons (SEPs).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Desmond Choo, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked if we could do more to take care of other groups of SEPs and freelancers who are more affected by the outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Pritam Singh raised the issue of bus drivers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The relevant Ministries will announce details for these other groups subsequently.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fourth, we have designed our measures to be able to reach enterprises as quickly as possible.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Seah Kian Peng and Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked if we could expedite the flow of the JSS payout to businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The disbursement of the JSS payout is operationally more complex due to the need to check and validate information on workers, employers and payment mode.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, we had initially projected for the JSS payout to reach companies by the end of July.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Employers using bank crediting will get the payout about a week earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enhancements to WCS will be provided in the second half of this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This way, we can also spread out our support for enterprises in a more sustained way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These measures in the package also come on top of the existing support schemes for firms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, there will be a WCS payout of more than $600 million to firms next month, based on the parameters announced in Budget 2018.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We should also look at the measures in the Stabilisation and Support Package in totality.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are providing a Property Tax Rebate to qualifying commercial properties, for which property owners will receive their revised tax bills in April, and refunds of any excess property tax paid by the end of May.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are also providing rental waivers for Government commercial tenants, the majority of which will apply to March and April rentals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the Corporate Income Tax Rebate, companies will receive their revised tax bills by the end of March.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These will provide not just financial relief but also help with enterprises' shorter-term cash flow needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many, including Mr Arasu Duraisamy, Ms Denise Phua, Dr Teo Ho Pin, Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Mr Alex Yam, have asked if we can do more for businesses and for a longer period of time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But if it does, for example, if the outbreak becomes a worldwide pandemic and the global economic impact is deeper and longer, we have the fiscal resources to do so and the will to act.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But, for now, let us go forth and make the fullest use of the support available out there before we review what more needs to be done.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As I have said, this is a fluid and fast moving situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are many stories of businesses and workers who are not just making full use of the Government's support, but taking it a step further to help each other and share the burden during this time of fear and uncertainty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Landlords, including CapitaLand and Frasers Property, have promised to pass on the Property Tax Rebate to affected tenants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The taxi and private hire car companies have taken steps in partnership with NTUC, the National Taxi Association, National Private Hire Vehicles Association and the Government to care for their drivers in their hour of need, even as they face challenges themselves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many businesses have also responded to the challenge with resilience and foresight, taking the opportunity to accelerate innovation and invest for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is exemplified by ParkRoyal at Kitchener Road.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I was impressed by the measures they are taking during this downtime to renovate the hotel, redesign processes, retrain their workers and redesign jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They are able to do this because even before the COVID-19 outbreak, they had been making plans to transform their operations to cope with manpower constraints.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Now, they are accelerating their transformation efforts, fully utilising the support that we are extending to them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Labour Movement has also been hard at work to help workers cope and emerge stronger from this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a time for all of us do our part.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Vikram Nair put it, the entire population needs to come together to weather the storm.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: People from all walks of life have come together to help others at a time when it is tempting to just look out for oneself.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In another example, Maturity Trust, a charity, is raising $500,000 under the Singapore Strong Fund to fund ground-up projects that help the community stay strong amid the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Delane Lim started the initiative Ops Hands-On to provide free masks and hand sanitisers to seniors and vulnerable residents in neighbourhoods across Singapore in collaboration with local Residents' Committees and Community Clubs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Students and staff from Wellington Primary School and several other schools made personalised cards to show support and appreciation for our frontline health workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Several Members of this House have shared heartwarming stories of how the community has banded together to cheer on our frontline workers as it combats the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Alex Yam talked about how volunteers in Yew Tee baked cookies for our frontline heroes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling talked about Singaporeans who wrote messages and prepared gifts to express their support and cheer them on.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our frontline health workers deserve our fullest support and encouragement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, our frontline workers, especially healthcare workers in the restructured hospitals, have shown outstanding courage and dedication.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They are out there making daily sacrifices to fight this war against the unknowns.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Seah Kian Peng put it, they act not because they have no fear but in spite of it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Senior Staff Manager, Ziadah Zainudin, has worked more than 12-hour days at Singapore General Hospital's Isolation Ward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Despite missing her birthday celebration with her family, she did not let COVID-19 stop her from doing her job.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Dr Melissa Tien responded to NCID's call for volunteers at its 24-hour Screening Centre, even though it meant sleeping in a different room from her husband and forgoing time with their two children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Dr Margaret Soon, the Director of Nursing at NCID and a veteran of SARS cancelled the family trip to work at the frontline.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But her family understood and supported her, including her daughter whom she was pregnant with during SARS 17 years ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The selflessness and commitment of our healthcare workers have shone through as they bravely care for those affected and tirelessly work to contain the spread of the virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They are an inspiration to all of us and their spirit of excellence has been recognised around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While we cannot thank them enough, we can show our appreciation and support in a tangible way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will include many healthcare officers in MOH and the restructured hospitals and some officers in other frontline agencies who have been directly involved.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This gesture, plus the many words of encouragement and acts of consideration and kindness, is our way to express to you that we salute you.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will win this war over the virus by fighting as One United People.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our citizens and institutions all play a part.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enterprises and senior management standing with unions and our workers, landlords supporting tenants, neighbours looking out for one another, political leaders working hand-in-hand with the Public Service and the people to do everything that will help.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will help us see these problems through together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore has been able to respond strongly and effectively to COVID-19 because there is strong trust between the people and the Government, and the sense that we are all in this together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government can make decisions quickly and carry them out effectively because Singaporeans have confidence that those responsible know what they are doing, care about their health and safety and share their worries and concerns.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We do not flinch from doing the right thing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will go the extra mile to help everyone of us come through this together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That is why people comply with stringent quarantine orders, people accept reassurances about masks, people feel safe and carry on with their lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The fundamental basis for this is trust and solidarity between the Government and the people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All MPs will also take a one-month cut in their allowance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The President has informed me that she will join in to take a similar one-month pay cut.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Senior Public Service officers will take a half-month pay cut.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the weeks and months to come, we will need to draw deeply on Singapore's reserves of resilience, trust and solidarity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This unity of purpose across our whole society is what will see us through these challenging times.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we conduct ourselves well in this crisis, we will replenish those Reserves and strengthen our resilience and unity for another generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Er Dr Lee Bee Wah said yesterday, in Singapore, "You Will Never Walk Alone".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2020 provides critical support to Singaporeans and businesses in this hour of need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are able to do so because we have managed our finances prudently and planned ahead to make sure that we always have enough to meet our people's needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 will not be the last challenge that we will face.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When this passes, we will continue to face the longer-term structural challenges of an ageing population, technological disruption, social inequality and climate change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to face sudden and unexpected situations, be it new virus outbreaks, threats to our security or financial crises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A responsible Government must ensure that the nation has the resources to meet these challenges and unexpected events, so that present and future generations of Singaporeans have the wherewithal to survive and thrive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Sitoh Yih Pin put it so well, we must always be ready.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Which path we choose and how we decide to share the burden of providing public services and building our collective future will define us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Will Singaporeans stand together to share the responsibility of providing for our collective future?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Or will we pass the cost to our children and grandchildren?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In many societies, such tensions have divided communities and created fault lines between millennials and Baby Boomers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, it is critical that we make a collective and informed decision to share the efforts and cost fairly, with citizens appreciating the reasons and values behind this decision.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many have been advocating that I give out more "sweets", more "M&Ms", more and more, be a generous "财神爷" or God of Fortune.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will be easier if I could deliver every Budget with just more good news, more spending on everything, more subsidies, more universal handouts and keep quiet about how we will pay for all of these.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has never been the Singapore way and I hope will never be.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, I will spend some time explaining the rationale and the hard choices and tradeoffs that we have to make.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope that Members will understand and appreciate the care and concerns behind the careful planning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we did not care as much for our collective future, we would not have thought so long and hard and expended so much political capital.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, I will explain why we should continue to steward our Reserves well, to safeguard the interests of future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, let me reiterate why we need to raise taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Nobody likes taxes, not even Ministers for Finance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a Government, our approach is to tax lightly, so that people can keep most of what they earn and so that they can decide how best to spend it for themselves, for their families or to donate it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But there are many critical national needs that are better met by government provision through taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include building up healthcare facilities and services, and providing subsidies to ensure that our healthcare needs are well taken care of.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include important priorities like mental health which Ms Anthea Ong spoke about passionately, and which will be discussed further during the Committee of Supply (COS) debate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I agree with the Member that good mental health is a foundation for well-being and resilience and we have already started including this as part of our work on human potential that we have added to our national research and development (R&D) budgets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include developing good and affordable preschool services and education to give all children, including our children with special needs, a good start in life and the best chance for success, regardless of background.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include building up the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) and Home Team to support our way of life in an era of emerging external, digital and terrorist threats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are all issues that many of us in this House care deeply about and made eloquent pitches for the Government to spend more on.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There must be a role for the Government to redistribute resources in the right way, so that everyone shares in the fruits of progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our way to do this is through schemes that enhance the capability of our people – through investments in education, healthcare and the provision of housing, as well as schemes to mitigate inequality like Workfare and Silver Support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked earlier whether I could provide more details about our expenditure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, I noticed that several MPs have gone through my Budget Annexes and looked at how much spending has increased for various Ministries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, let me just take this occasion to cover one important area, an important area because the big shift in public expenditure in the next decade will be in healthcare spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will grow significantly as our population ages and as medical technology improves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Now, let me show Members a chart that shows Singapore's and other countries' public health expenditure as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) against the share of the total population that is over 65 years old.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the "x" axis is the percentage of total population which is more than 65 years old; and on the vertical axis is public health expenditure as a percentage of GDP.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The triangle shows the year 2000 and the circle the year 2015.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, in other words, a period of 15 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When Members look at the green line, South Korea; the purple line, the US; New Zealand, Germany the blue line; and Japan, the yellow line, you can see how they have all gone up sharply as population ages and as technology improves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a percentage of GDP, the US is at the highest at almost 14%, Germany at about 9% and Japan at also about 8% or 9%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The dotted line represents the future, projections by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we did a similar projection to look at what would Singapore's numbers be, if we used MOH's projections.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And that is the bottom, the lower dotted line.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And then the upper dotted line is if we were to use OECD's methodology or OECD's trends.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the share of seniors increases over time, public health expenditure has simply increased.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as I said, medical technologies will continue to improve.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This trend has been played out in Singapore and all the other countries, as shown in this chart.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the past two decades, our healthcare expenditure has grown rapidly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since 2010, we have opened or expanded eight hospitals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have built two new polyclinics and redeveloped three existing ones.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The spending is not just on the infrastructure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For every hospital that you build, the capital expenditure (capex) that we put in, the operating expenditure (opex) is even more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, it just tells you the trend that we are heading towards.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And healthcare spending is not just about treating the sick.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is also about giving our seniors a better quality of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The number of cataract operations per year on seniors increased from around 10,000 in the year 2000 to almost 30,000 last year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such procedures were less common in the past because people did not live as long as they do today to need them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And because of advances in medical sciences, previously incurable diseases, like cancer, can be better managed, and patients can continue to live for more years with a good quality of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Going forward, healthcare spending will continue to grow significantly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, while this is a very good thing that our people are living longer, we must be prepared that we will have to spend more on healthcare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we expect public healthcare spending to grow by around one percentage point of GDP over the 15 years from 2015 to 2030.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is, in fact, as I mentioned to you earlier, less than the average increases projected in the OECD countries, partly because of our efforts to keep healthcare costs sustainable and because Singaporeans have increasingly adopted healthier lifestyles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But our healthcare spending may rise by more than this one percentage point if medical costs rise throughout the world and we do not bring problems like obesity and diabetes under control.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Lim Biow Chuan said, Singaporeans must understand that increased spending on healthcare must come from somewhere.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some have wondered if we can spend less or spend more efficiently.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, it is not just about how much we spend but how well we spend.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we achieve good outcomes at a lower cost than many other countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In health, we have the highest life expectancy in the world – almost 85 years – but still spend less of our GDP compared to other countries, as Members can see in this chart, our life expectancy compared against public health expenditure as a percentage of GDP of various countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, former World Bank President Jim Yong Kim said that it was "stunning" that Singapore had achieved its current outcomes despite relatively low spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, I will thank our people and our healthcare workers for taking care of their own health and for doing such a good job.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Similarly, for education, our 15-year-olds do well in international indices of educational attainment like the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) test despite Singapore spending less than other countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are able to achieve this only because of a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the Government’s part, we have carefully designed our education and healthcare systems to deliver good services in a cost-effective manner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have dedicated and passionate educators who believe in developing every child to their fullest potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have committed healthcare professionals who believe in delivering the best care to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is strong support for Singaporean families from community groups and social service agencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And Singaporeans themselves play an important role in taking responsibility for their own learning and health.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are always looking for ways to improve outcomes in a cost-effective manner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Lawrence Wong will elaborate on some of these efforts during the Ministry of Finance's (MOF's) COS debate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But efficiency savings will never be enough to fully offset the growth in healthcare spending as the population ages and medical sciences improve.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har shared that some Singaporeans have questioned the need to raise revenues to meet the expenditures I mentioned, pointing at surpluses seen in this term of Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But our healthcare spending needs are not one-off needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We cannot hope to keep on being so pleasantly surprised.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Things can very quickly swing in the opposite direction, as we have seen from the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must ensure that we have enough resources to meet our people’s needs, driven by structural factors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Otherwise, we will find ourselves short and have to raise taxes or cut spending in difficult times, precisely when businesses and people need a boost.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Planning ahead entails being honest with ourselves and with citizens, and having the discipline to raise revenues in a timely manner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, it is fair for everyone to bear some part of the cost.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is about all of us taking shared responsibility to pay for our needs and our society’s needs and sharing in the effort to provide for them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is at the same time a Singapore-style GST that comes with offsets to ensure that those with lower incomes pay much less than those who are well-off.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, at the individual level, many Singaporeans are willing to chip in to meet these needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In my conversations with my constituents, I have asked if they would be willing to contribute just 20 cents more out of $10 that they spend a day, if this would help to ensure that their healthcare needs and those of their parents were adequately taken care of.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many were willing to accept this small cost for peace of mind.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The compact does not change when we project it to the national level.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is ultimately about us collectively chipping in to look after the healthcare needs of our families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Each generation must pay for its own spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har and some others have asked if we should raise income and wealth taxes instead of GST.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, we have been doing so in recent years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2010, we made our property tax regime progressive by introducing higher tax rates on owner-occupied residential properties with higher Annual Values.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We enhanced the progressivity of our property tax system in 2013, with higher property tax rates for homes and non-owner-occupied residential properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2015, we raised the top marginal personal income tax rate from 20% to 22%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The following year, we introduced a cap on the personal income tax relief to make our regime more progressive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2018, we raised the Buyer’s Stamp Duty for residential properties in excess of $1 million in value.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In all this time, when we were raising income and wealth taxes to support the country’s growing expenditure, the GST rate remained at 7%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The last time we raised it was in 2007, more than 10 years ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we should bear in mind that there is a limit to raising income taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we keep raising income taxes, it will eventually hurt middle-class Singaporeans, who presently pay very light income taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will also risk losing our ability to attract talent and keep our own talents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Ms Tin Pei Ling said, "Talents beget talents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is a virtuous cycle to this." It is important to have a critical mass of talent in Singapore to create jobs and economic vibrancy, which will benefit Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That said, as important as raising the GST is, it is only one way to meet our revenue needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But the increase in annual Government healthcare spending alone that I mentioned already exceeds the amount of additional revenue.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we will continue to adjust our income and wealth taxes to raise revenue in a progressive and fair manner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We should keep international tax developments in mind as we review these taxes, both personal income tax as well as corporate income tax.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Cedric Foo and Mr Henry Kwek noted, there are ongoing international discussions to revise tax rules under the BEPS project.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hub economies with small markets like Singapore stand to lose corporate income tax revenue if the new rules are adopted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is because the new rules allocate taxes to where the customers are rather than where the underlying economic activity is conducted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses are highly mobile in today’s global economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Companies, especially multinationals, have the flexibility to relocate their businesses out of Singapore to elsewhere.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, Mr Pritam Singh asked me earlier about the status of BEPS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Well, in fact, I am glad that MOF officials have been very involved in this international discussion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some of these discussions are confidential in nature.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But I assure Mr Pritam Singh that hub economies will have to bear some negative in this exercise for the reasons I mentioned – where you tax the activity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Is it where the consumers are or where the underlying economic activities are?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That change in principle alone, you can work out what the effects will be for us as a hub economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We, therefore, need to strike a fine balance between our corporate income tax rate and economic competitiveness.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ultimately, how much we spend depends on how much we collectively have to pay in the form of taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This chart shows the standard GST or value-added tax rates that other jurisdictions adopt, compared with our future rate of 9%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Among the Nordics, for example, the value-added tax rates are as high as 25%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They also have top personal income tax rates as high as over 50%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They have accepted higher taxes as the price for their higher social spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we seek to keep the GST rate low, we have to make tradeoffs as we increase our spending for our healthcare and other needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many countries in the region and elsewhere have standard GST rates that exceed 9%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even Saudi Arabia, a country with huge oil reserves, is carefully planning ahead and introduced a 5% value-added tax from 2018.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, let me address concerns raised about the impact of the GST hike on the lower-income and the impact on cost of living.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In designing our fiscal system, we have always sought to achieve a fair and progressive balance where the better-off contribute more and the lower-income receive more support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This overall philosophy is a key consideration in how we design the GST and how we will implement the GST hike.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is why I have announced an Assurance Package to cushion the increase for all Singaporeans when the revised GST rate kicks in by 2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This provides a bigger and thicker cushion to the lower- and middle-income, including many seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There have been questions over the logic of raising GST and providing a $6 billion Assurance Package for GST, and whether we can just delay or not even increase the GST rate at all.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Delaying the GST increase is not the same as raising the GST and providing offsets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is because of the design of our system and the resulting incidence of the GST burden.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we flow part of the GST revenue back in the form of a GST Voucher that gives more to those who need it most, particularly the lower-income and retiree households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a permanent part of our system and will be enhanced when the GST hike takes place.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The GST Voucher reduces the net GST borne by lower- and middle-income households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Net GST is the amount of GST borne by each household, after accounting for the GST Voucher they receive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the GST Voucher, the bottom 40% of resident households are estimated to account for less than 10% of the net GST borne by all households and individuals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the other hand, a significant part of the net GST is borne by foreigners and higher-income households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked what proportion of the GST is borne by this group.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is after taking into account GST refunded under the Tourist Refund Scheme for goods bought here for consumption abroad.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is partly because foreigners do not benefit from the GST Voucher and offsets, which are available only to Singaporean households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When we eventually increase the GST rate to 9%, foreigners pay the higher rate immediately.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In contrast, Singaporeans receive offsets to cushion the impact, through both the permanent GST Voucher and the Assurance Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as I said, for some households it is equivalent to not having the GST increase for five years, and for some even 10 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All in, the GST increase, implemented together with the Assurance Package, will achieve several different objectives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Most importantly, we delay the impact of the increase on most Singaporeans, by five years or more, and even longer for the lower-income.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can start collecting revenue from foreigners residing in Singapore and tourists, and our businesses make the changes to their IT systems only once.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The GST is only one part of our fiscal system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When you look at the system of taxes and benefits as a whole, it is a progressive one.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The top 10% of taxpayers pay about 80% of our personal income tax revenue.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As shown in this chart, lower- and middle-income households receive proportionately more benefits than the taxes they pay, whereas higher-income groups contribute a far higher share of taxes than the share of benefits they receive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, as you can see, the top 20% pay 55% of the taxes and receive 12% of the benefits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The bottom 20% pay 9% of the taxes and receive 28% of the benefits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, let me summarise what I have explained in three points.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we care for fellow Singaporeans and want to support them, especially in healthcare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To fund this spending, we need to raise the GST.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will take collective responsibility to look after one another.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Raising the GST, a broad-based tax to meet a broad-based need, is a sustainable approach.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we ensure that we are fair when the GST is raised.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Reserves are our nest egg, borne of hard work and discipline.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During the earlier years of economic catch-up, Singapore experienced fast growth and had a young working population.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our founding fathers made the decision to save the country’s surpluses and invest it for the long term to build up Singapore’s nest egg.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They could have just spent it to gain immediate political advantage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But they were principled and had the long-term interests of our people and our nation at heart.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a highly unusual and a very fortunate position.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Most advanced countries, shown in the lower half of this chart, pay about 2% of their GDP in debt servicing of accumulated debt.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They collect taxes to pay off the debts of previous generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As you can see from that graph, the red line is the US and the green line on top is France, and Germany in between at about 2%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In Singapore, as shown in the top half of the chart, it is the opposite.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Reserves generate substantial returns, which help to keep our taxes low.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In other words, in most advanced countries, citizens today pay for the spending of the past generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Citizens today enjoy the benefits of the savings from the past, thanks to the foresight and policies of our founding generation of leaders and people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Tell me, in which other country are citizens able to reap the benefits of past savings in this way?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, let us never forget that what we have inherited is very unusual and very precious.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us be responsible and steward this properly for our future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Leon Perera asked if we can slow the rate of growth of our Reserves and release more funds to invest in our people and companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am sure he is aware that in 2008, we introduced the Net Investment Returns framework and, in 2015, we passed a constitutional amendment to add Temasek in the framework.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This has resulted in a significant increase in NIRC that has gone towards various spending, including investments in our capabilities to generate future growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Put it in another way, today at $17 billion, the NIRC is able to cover almost the combined budget of the Ministry of Education (MOE) and and the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More importantly, our Reserves give us the confidence, as a small country with no natural resources of any kind, to deal with the ups and downs in the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is why we have a robust set of rules to safeguard and manage the use of Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The President plays a critical role in guarding against profligate spending and to ensure proper use of our Past Reserves to safeguard Singapore’s interest when needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During the Global Financial Crisis more than a decade ago, with global financial markets in turmoil and governments around the world scrambling to protect bank deposits, then-President SR Nathan approved the provision of $150 billion from our Past Reserves to guarantee bank deposits in Singapore from October 2008 to December 2010.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I was the Managing Director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) at that point.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And I can tell you that our officers in MAS worked day and night to safeguard the stability of the banking system, and were totally conscious that we were using our Past Reserves as a guarantee, but we were also confident that the guarantee will be put to good use because it is to stabilise the confidence of depositors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, throughout that period, we had a very difficult time but, towards the end of it, we did not have a single bank run.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2009, then-President SR Nathan approved a draw of $4.9 billion from our Past Reserves to fund the Resilience Package to help us overcome the Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A year later, after the economy rebounded sharply, the Government decided to return the money used to our Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It did not have to, but did so, to maintain the discipline that has allowed this unusual move in the first place.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, we have not had to tap our Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But it was the same spirit of prudence that allowed us to have enough surplus this term to provide the fiscal support for our economy and our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But if the situation deteriorates significantly and calls for us to tap on our Past Reserves, I will make a case to the President to seek her approval to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can do the easy thing and avoid the pain for ourselves today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can decide not to raise GST to pay for our own spending, but to tap on our Reserves and its investment returns instead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But by doing so, we will soon deprive future generations of the benefits that we enjoy today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During a Parliamentary hearing in 2001 on the Bill to allow the Government to use part of the returns of investment from our Reserves, our founding Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew said, “What is the deepest obligation of any government?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is not to the present, and certainly not the past, but to the future.” Let me repeat that: "What is the deepest obligation of any government?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is not to the present, and certainly not the past, but to the future".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have a duty not just to those who make their views known today, but also to the young and the future Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They are not here today to represent their interests because they are not born yet!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we have a responsibility to them, and to take decisions which are difficult for us but which will safeguard their interests.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us continue to keep the discipline and keep the faith and promise to future generations of Singaporeans, by stewarding our Reserves well in our time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Climate change is another area where we may not live to reap the benefits of our decisions but our children will.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Climate change threatens our very existence as a small low-lying island state.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But Singapore has always risen to the challenge in the face of adversity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have never accepted our fate or our starting circumstances meekly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Dealing with our water and land constraints has made us leaders in water technology and urban planning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our manpower constraints constantly push us to automate, digitalise and be more productive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Now, we have a plan to address our carbon and energy constraints.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are meeting the challenge head-on, with an ambitious plan to tackle climate change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are not only securing our coasts but also transforming our sources of food and water and remaking our entire economy and city for a green and sustainable future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MTI and MEWR will prepare our economy and society for the low-carbon transition by working with various stakeholders and partners to reduce our greenhouse gas emissions and seize opportunities in the circular economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) is working on our vision to phase out internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles and have all vehicles run on cleaner energy by 2040.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of National Development is making efforts to make our towns greener and more sustainable, and transform Singapore into a City in Nature.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are ambitious plans and we are bringing our R&D investments in urban solutions and sustainability to bear to realise this vision.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The respective Ministers will speak more on these efforts and, in fact, Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean will speak on this in the COS debate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope their explanations will give Mr Dennis Tan a fuller picture of all that we are doing to tackle this serious challenge.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He and Mr Yee Chia Hsing, Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Murali Pillai gave their perspectives on the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We already have the Vehicular Emissions Scheme and, in this Budget, I announced the EV Early Adoption Incentive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help to close the cost premiums between EVs and ICE vehicles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over time, as technology improves, we expect the cost differential to close further.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, while we want to encourage drivers to replace their ICE vehicles with EVs, we should bear in mind that the cleanest and most efficient mode of transport remains public transport.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A car-lite vision that Mr Khaw Boon Wan has articulated continues to be the main focus of our transport policy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a whole-of-society, multi-generational effort and its success will depend on all Singaporeans taking action.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am very happy that many young Singaporeans are passionate about this cause and want to be part of the solution.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are in for the long haul, and our journey to tackle climate change will span 50, even 100 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is, as one commentator pointed out, a big audacious goal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But if we do not have the courage and determination to tackle challenges that threaten our very existence, what is our ambition for?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such long-term investments, together with our Reserves, represent our commitment to future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we take the long-term view and each generation plays its part, Singapore can face the future with confidence, the confidence that we will always have the capacity to overcome every challenge, be it a virus outbreak, recession or rising sea levels; confidence that we will be able to provide for our families and community; and confidence that our children will have the best chance of a better life, come what may.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Now, let me touch on how we will strengthen the social compact and continue to fulfil the promise of opportunities for all in changing times.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Denise Phua, Assoc Prof Walter Theseira and others spoke on the need to tackle inequality and preserve social mobility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore was founded on a vision of a "just and equal society" – broad-based prosperity and equal opportunities for all – a society where every Singaporean, regardless of background and starting point, has a good chance to do better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, this remains this Government's mission to enable all Singaporeans to enjoy the fruits of growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, we have made good progress in fulfilling this goal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we will confront complex new challenges ahead, including the pressures of technological and demographic change and the growing inequality of starting points, as our society matures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our response to these challenges will define us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A growing number of societies have responded by turning inwards from the world, even as they grow more polarised and divided within.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For Singapore to stay successful, we must have the courage to take a different path.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to anticipate and respond to change, plan for the long term, and find practical solutions to create better lives for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to stay open and connected to the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to foster trust in society, a point which Prof Yaacob Ibrahim spoke yesterday.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Above all, we must stay united as one people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our unity is what makes Singapore's story exceptional.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will require us to put in place synergistic fiscal, monetary and structural policies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With sensible and prudent fiscal policies that promote growth and social equity, appropriate monetary policy to promote macroeconomic stability to maintain price stability and promote steady growth, and structural policies that expand the capacity of our firms and labour force for growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
