text: The global economy is undergoing tectonic shifts today and many countries face a new economic landscape.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore must move fast to secure growth and jobs in the next bound, or face irrelevance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we are moving quickly to secure our external economic space, to create new opportunities and room for manoeuvre in an increasingly fragmented economic order.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have enhanced our economic connectivity through our network of trade agreements and avoidance of double taxation agreements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have also created new linkages with other economies through digital agreements and new platforms and networks, such as the Networked Trade Platform and Global Innovation Alliance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These moves diversify our markets and supply chains and have made us more resilient in times of rising protectionism.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we are increasing the capacity of our enterprises and industries to innovate, grow and transform.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Ong Teng Koon pointed out, building up strong local capabilities and ecosystems for innovation is critical to our economic success and resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are, therefore, helping enterprises to deepen their capabilities at every stage of their growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, I am very happy to hear Mr Teo Ser Luck sharing his personal entrepreneurship journey by making use of the grant but cautioning not to overdo it or you will destroy the spirit of enterprise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To strengthen our competitive advantages, we have expanded our R&D investments into new areas and technologies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through these investments, we are harnessing the latest technologies to transform our manufacturing and services sectors and creating new growth clusters in areas, such as urban solutions and sustainability, health and human potential and agri-food tech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have brought industry and the research community together to experiment and collaborate with the Government in test-bedding solutions in areas like urban mobility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But the success of each ITM comes down to the strength of leadership in our enterprises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Business leaders must have the mental agility and dynamism to experiment and the resourcefulness to overcome constraints.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That is why, in this Budget, we are supporting business leaders through the Enterprise Leadership for Transformation (ELT) programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our institutes of higher learning (IHLs), such as the Singapore Management University, have joined hands with Enterprise Singapore to support this effort.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enterprise Singapore will bring more partners on board the ELT programme in the coming months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the industry level, partnership among businesses is key.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, even as businesses compete with one another and seek to differentiate themselves, cooperation can help them do better, such as by forming alliances to capture opportunities overseas or collaborating to testbed sector-wide solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And this is exemplified by the Singapore Manufacturing Federation, which, under Mr Douglas Foo's leadership, is making a concerted effort to transform the manufacturing sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A joint venture among five poultry producers and processors, the Hub's smart factory will deploy emerging technologies to increase productivity by 26% and production capacity by 70%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By working together, these poultry producers were able to achieve the scale needed to transform a labour-intensive process.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, though they remain competitors, they certainly did not chicken out from working together!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Minister Josephine Teo reminded us, economic transformation is not painless.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses must be willing to bear the transitional pains, to be creative and resourceful, and to seize opportunities where others see challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Encouragingly, we are starting to see the fruits of our moves to transform the economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Productivity has grown in the last three years and our enterprises are entering new markets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are also seeing continued confidence and investments in Singapore despite economic headwinds.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These show that we are taking steps in the right direction.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Most importantly, our efforts are creating more and better jobs for all.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Above all, locals are benefiting from the jobs created.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And more locals are employed in higher paying jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2010, 37% of full-time employed local workers earned a gross monthly income, excluding employer Central Provident Fund (CPF), of at least $4,000 in today's dollars, adjusting for inflation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2019, 51% of local workers earned at least $4,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, 51% in 2019 compared to 37% in 2010.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At its heart, economic transformation involves the courage to brave transitional pains as we change the way we do things.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And if we can all move forward with this can-do spirit of initiative and partnership that we have shown in the past weeks, I am confident that we will build strong firms that can grow and compete in the global arena and create good jobs for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As our economy undergoes structural changes, our labour market is also facing profound structural changes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As our population ages, our resident workforce will shrink rapidly, tightening our labour market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: People are living longer and expect to have longer, even multiple, careers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And rapid advances in technology and business models will bring more frequent and disruptive changes to skills required at jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Prof Lim Sun Sun and Mr Christopher de Souza put it, change is the only constant and we cannot run away from it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our collective mentality towards upskilling must change from nice-to-have to must-do, a point that Mr Teo Ser Luck also mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are responding to these changes by taking a three-prong tripartite approach with the Government, workers and enterprises working in close concert to deal with these structural changes in our labour market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The first prong is for the Government to invest in critical enablers of skills upgrading and in career support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have shifted our approach to education to one that enables learning throughout life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are investing heavily in our IHLs to build up a future-ready ecosystem.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with other training providers, our IHLs offer a large suite of Continuing Education and Training (CET) courses, many of which are industry-relevant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And together with those provided by other training providers, our IHLs' CET courses provide a key pathway for individuals to gain skills and confidence to make career transitions and to realise their aspirations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government subsidises these courses heavily, with subsidy rates as high as 90% of course fees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond education, we are enhancing our support to help workers make the transitions smoothly, and this is especially important for mid-career workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must turn these anxieties into actions that improve lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Adapt and Grow initiative helps workers find opportunities, refresh their skills and transition to new roles faster.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) help workers take on new job roles and our career coaches give career guidance and help jobseekers secure new jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When I visited Workforce Singapore's (WSG's) Careers Connect last September, I met Mr Lam Kong Chai, 58 years old.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Lam had been job hunting for two years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With WSG's help, he was hired as the Finance Director at Asia-Europe Foundation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: His hiring manager herself had previously received career advice from WSG and approached WSG to fill the role that Mr Lam took on.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In turn, Mr Lam worked with WSG to fill a vacancy in his team.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, all three individuals ended up getting jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The outcomes of our Adapt and Grow initiative are encouraging.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: About nine in 10 of those who went through our PCPs remained in employment 24 months after placement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And about seven in 10 also earned higher wages after starting their new jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our coaches work with about 27,000 jobseekers every year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2018, they managed to place about seven in 10 jobseekers into new jobs within six months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These will be discussed further during the COS debate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second prong of this approach is to enable our workers to take ownership of their own learning and growth through the SkillsFuture movement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Initiatives, such as the SkillsFuture Credit, encourage each individual to take charge of their learning throughout life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with Government subsidies for CET courses, our workers can access quality programmes with low or zero out-of-pocket payment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Take, for example, a Big Data Engineering for Analytics course which costs about $4,500 before Government subsidies at a SkillsFuture Singapore-appointed CET centre.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A Singaporean worker aged 40 or older enjoys a 90% course subsidy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The remaining $450 can be fully met from the worker's existing SkillsFuture Credit or the top-up that this worker will get in this Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, the SkillsFuture Credit works in conjunction with the broader CET ecosystem of support that we have built up.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope this assures members like Mr Arasu Duraisamy and Ms Irene Quay, who raised queries on the credit and concerns about whether it can really make a difference.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Labour Movement is innovating and exercising collective leadership to strengthen individual workers' efforts, for example, the Job Security Council initiated by Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng as well as the Company Training Committees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third prong of our tripartite approach is to get our enterprises to step up their own enterprise transformation and, in tandem, to redesign jobs and upgrade their workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Ms Jessica Tan pointed out, leadership must come from employers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Ong Teng Koon was concerned that it may be hard for SMEs to take workers away from the day-to-day business needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, there is no better time than now to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many businesses are already using this downtime to accelerate change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This three-prong approach, building on our tripartite framework, is our structural response to the structural changes in the labour market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are able to do this because we have been investing significantly in our education upstream, to build a strong foundation to enable our people's success.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Investing upstream means supporting every child to reach their fullest potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, over 90% of the total cost of educating our children from primary to pre-university level is subsidised by the Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Then, when they go on to an IHL, which most students do, they get an additional $15,000 to $22,000 in subsidies per year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Students from lower- and middle-income households receive additional bursaries and subsidies on top of this, which I have enhanced in this Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are now investing significantly more in affordable, quality preschool education while giving low-income families additional support for early childhood development through KidSTART.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are also equipping young Singaporeans with skills they need for the new economy, including cross-cultural skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this Budget, I announced our "70-70" target, Asia-Ready Exposure Programme and enhancements to the Global Ready Talent Programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Another key area where we invest upstream is housing, so that everyone has a home.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We provide generous housing subsidies to keep Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats affordable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: New HDB flats are sold at prices below their market rate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over and above subsidies, we provide substantial housing grants, depending on the income of the buyers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Eligible first-time buyers who buy resale flats get grants of up to $160,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, a resale flat can cost less than five times the annual salary of a median-income household.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is much lower than international cities like Hong Kong, Sydney, London or New York.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This chart compares the median house price as a ratio of the median household income in major cities before accounting for grants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By intervening upstream in these areas, we provide a foundation of broad-based opportunities that enables everyone to earn their own success.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a result, Singaporeans have been able to enjoy the fruits of progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Now, I will show Members another chart that shows resident-employed households have experienced sustained real income growth at the median, growing by 3.7% per year over the last decade.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members can see the numbers for yourselves versus other developed economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While the data are not perfectly comparable internationally, the growth that we have experienced is higher than that of many advanced economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In short, our approach in these changing times is to take structural measures to strengthen opportunities at every stage of life, with individuals, employers, unions all doing their part.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For this to succeed, the change must come from within.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For all the programmes that the Government puts in place, each individual will have to take responsibility for their own growth and learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we can all take on a mindset of growth and a spirit of resilience, we can be assured that we will emerge stronger and better to face the future ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have spoken on our first two strategies of transforming our economy and developing our people to enable opportunities for all.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Budget provides further support for those who may face greater pressures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, some face difficulties with employment and ensuring that growth in their income keeps pace with inflation, despite their best efforts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira, Mr Zainal Sapari and Mr Png Eng Huat have spoken on the vulnerabilities of low-wage workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Care and Support Package, which includes Grocery Vouchers to provide help with daily necessities, will help them and their families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It builds on our efforts in recent years to strengthen social support and safety nets for low-income workers and their families through enhancements to Workfare, the Progressive Wage Model, and ComCare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The mayors and the five Community Development Councils (CDCs) have local assistance schemes to support the heartlands, as pointed out by Mayor Low Yen Ling.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These local efforts, done in partnership with community partners, local merchants and many others, bring warmth and support from fellow Singaporeans and business owners who are also our neighbours.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These enhancements go beyond inflation growth to provide stronger support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Saktiandi Sapaat spoke about the stresses faced by middle-class families that are "sandwiched" financially because they have to care for both their children and their elderly parents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Louis Ng, Ms Yip Pin Xiu, Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Darryl David also pointed out that they may face pressures in terms of time from balancing their caregiving responsibilities and work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, we also announced measures to support parenthood and caregiving, including enhancements to preschool subsidies, and the Home Caregiving Grant under MOH's Caregiver Support Action Plan.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Supporting and strengthening families will always be a priority for us and we will continue to look at how we can do so effectively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These issues will be discussed further at the COS debate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These measures come on top of the extensive subsidies that I mentioned earlier in education, healthcare and public housing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Middle-income households – those in the middle 20% by household income – benefit substantially from this system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2019, they received $2 in benefits for every $1 in tax paid.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Overall measures that we have put in place over the past decade to provide good jobs for our people, develop them at all stages of life and support the vulnerable, have made a decisive impact in narrowing the income gap.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is encouraging, but our work is not done.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will always continue to look at practical, effective moves to tackle inequality and ensure that all Singaporeans progress together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Critically, businesses and the community have growing roles to play.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A caring and cohesive society begins with everyday acts of kindness, of philanthropy and volunteerism.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are better antidotes to inequality than the politics of class warfare that we have seen around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Miss Cheng Li Hui put it, graciousness and kindness are, indeed, part of our Singapore spirit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is much we can do to build an inclusive society for all, including those with special needs and persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar and Mdm Rahayu Mahzam reminded us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is why it has been my priority to support, enable and amplify the efforts of citizens and businesses to help those in need through Singapore Together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2018, individuals collectively donated $2.1 billion through registered organisations, more than double the $960 million donated in 2008.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Each donor gave, on average, about $660, which is more than twice the amount in 2008.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, one in two businesses in Singapore gives back through philanthropy and volunteering.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our social service agencies have been doing good work for the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They, too, have been going through their own transformation journeys, building up technological capabilities to be more effective in helping those in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the Cerebral Palsy Alliance Singapore has invested in an anti-gravity treadmill, so that clients can practise moving and walking in a fall-free environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Going forward, we will partner the community to support more of such capability-development efforts, through the Community Capability Trust that I announced in this Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such investments and partnerships will help social service agencies to overcome the manpower constraints that Ms Joan Pereira spoke on.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This good work is not just confined to organised sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many MPs have also shared stories embodying the spirit of Singapore Together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and many others shared about the spontaneous and thoughtful acts in many housing estates, such as fellow residents coming together to bottle hand sanitisers and placing them in lifts for residents to use.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And I would say that we can go a step further, that the democracy of deeds means each of us taking action to realise the good.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is also very inspiring to hear how several Members of this House are taking the lead to serve our community in their own diverse ways.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira, an economist, has been doing a lot of work on the labour market; Mr Douglas Foo leading the SMF effort; Mr Terence Ho, using the arts to enable and empower individuals from underprivileged backgrounds; Ms Anthea Ong, fighting to raise awareness of mental illness among us and to promote mental wellness; Ms Irene Quay, who has served the public passionately in healthcare, volunteering in a hospice despite her many commitments; Ms Yip Pin Xiu, who is inspiring young athletes and showing Singaporeans and the world what it truly means; Mr Mohamed Irshad, who is fostering religious harmony and helping to build a more caring society; Prof Lim Sun Sun for her work on the need to educate our young even better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as Ms Denise Phua said, there are so many other areas that we can work together to take action to build a better society and improve lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: She herself has taken so much action and devoted so much effort in uplifting people with special needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is how we should rise to the challenge of inequality in this day and age – by coming together as one people to uplift the less privileged amongst us, with the state providing strong foundations of opportunity and support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I do apologise that this is longer than what everyone had been expecting.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But there have been so many good stories I thought it is bears telling.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, thank you all for your patience in this Singapore Together effort.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: You sit together to listen to my long speech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In Mandarin):   	There is a Chinese saying, "前人种树，后人乘凉", which means that the current generation plants the seeds which eventually grow into trees that provide shade for the next generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Reserves are akin to a tree planted by our earlier generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, this tree is well-grown and we are able to take shelter under it, benefiting from the stable income that it generates for our country.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To draw on the Reserves or become overly reliant on NIRC to meet recurrent expenditure is akin to damaging or even cutting down the tree.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our recurrent expenditure, especially on healthcare, is increasing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to continue developing healthcare facilities and providing healthcare services to ensure that elderly Singaporeans are well taken care of.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Not only does this allow us to increase revenue in a sustainable and effective manner, it also reflects our value of collective responsibility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we raise the GST rate, we will ensure that our taxes remain fair.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The permanent GST Voucher Scheme mitigates the impact of GST on lower- and middle-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, the Assurance Package for GST will offset at least five years' worth of additional GST expenses incurred for most Singaporean households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For lower-income Singaporeans, the Package can offset about 10 years of the additional GST expenses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When we eventually increase the GST rate, tourists and foreigners residing in Singapore will pay the 9% GST immediately.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, a significant part of net GST is borne by foreigners and higher-income households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Foreigners and higher-income households are estimated to account for over 60% of the net GST borne by all households and individuals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, we are also committed to ensuring that our future generations continue to enjoy a sustainable living environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The risks brought about by climate change are one of the challenges that we must tackle.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As an island nation, Singapore is highly susceptible to the impact brought about by rising sea levels and floods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides managing the impact of climate change, we must continue to build a liveable, caring and vibrant home for ourselves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the face of the COVID-19 outbreak, we must unite as one people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To express our respect and gratitude, the Government will be providing up to one additional month of special bonus for frontline healthcare workers and public servants who are directly battling with the COVID-19 disease and facing higher risks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, we will provide a one-off grant for Public Health Preparedness Clinics.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During this difficult period, our Government leaders will stand in solidarity will all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, all political officeholders will take a one-month cut in their salary, and all MPs will take a one-month cut in their allowance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: President Halimah Yaacob is also supportive of the move and has volunteered to take a one-month pay cut.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Senior Public Service officers will similarly take a half-month pay cut.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we progress, we will meet many challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some will be for the longer term, while some will be more immediate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I can understand that Singaporeans are worried about the impact of the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, as we tackle the immediate challenges, we must also set our sights on the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Zaobao commentator Giam Meng Tuck aptly described this Budget as three prescriptions, namely, "定心丸" (assurance pill), "润肺散" (lung moisturising powder, to ameliorate ill-effects) and "提神三味汤" (three-flavoured soup to invigorate the spirit).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The values conveyed by the Chinese saying, "前人种树，后人乘凉", remains a cornerstone of Singapore's long-term fiscal planning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have to continue protecting and nurturing the tree planted by earlier generations, to take care of our future generations and ensure that generations of Singaporeans after us will have enough resources to face future challenges, seize opportunities and build a better Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, I will now conclude in English.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We began our journey as a nation with a mission – seeking the welfare and happiness of Singaporeans in a more just and equal society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through rain or shine, we have never wavered from this mission.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We live in a time of change and uncertainty today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But it is precisely in such times that our strength and resolve as a nation shine most brightly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us not be paralysed and divided by anxiety and fear, but let us be energised and united by optimism and a common vision for tomorrow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us rise to the occasion and overcome the COVID-19 outbreak together, stepping up to take care of one another in these trying times.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us share the effort to build our future and nation together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us build a sustainable Singapore, where we and our children can live our best lives in a safe, green and livable environment, for all time and seasons to come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us grow as a city of possibilities – an open, globally-connected city, where each Singaporean can live to the fullest, and bring our aspirations, hopes and potential to life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us continue to build a society of opportunity for all where we have the freedom to determine our own destiny, based not on our starting points, but through our own choices and efforts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And let us continue to foster a caring and cohesive community, living as equals, uplifting the most vulnerable among us and taking care of our fellow men and women.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All of this is within our reach, if we work as One Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With collective action and leadership at all levels of society and with our diverse strengths and passions combined, we can build a society that we can all be proud of.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the spirit of Singapore Together, and it is alive today, as shown by many Singaporeans, including Members of this House, who are leading change in diverse ways.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Above all, let us never stop thinking for tomorrow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the long and never-ending journey of nation-building, each generation of Singaporeans are relay runners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: May we always take good care of what we have inherited, run our best race and pass on a better future to those who come after us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Budget is about one step in this long race, building upon the sweat and toil of generations who have run the race before us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It seeks to do right by Singaporeans, both present and future, through the financial plans and provisions that we make today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us unite and forge ahead as One Singapore to build a better Singapore for tomorrow. "Singapore Together, Majulah Forever!"
